strengths: Well-motivated formulation that decomposes complex 3D mesh editing into 2D image editing, single-image 3D mesh generation, and seamless local fusion, bypassing common failure modes of SDS optimization such as over-smoothing and geometric collapse.

The proposed Poisson Geometry Blending effectively leverages blended normal maps applied to a hybrid SDF/mesh representation, successfully resolving seam discontinuities and topology artifacts from naive mesh boolean operations.

The Poisson Texture Harmonization strategy—combining distribution-aware color alignment, gradient preservation, and boundary distance weighting—effectively eliminates visual seam artifacts and color disparity between the existing and newly generated mesh regions.
The framework exhibits good versatility, readily accommodating diverse editing interfaces such as text-driven editing and user-guided drag-based deformations (via LightningDrag).
weaknesses: The evaluation scale is very limited: the quantitative and qualitative evaluation is conducted on a dataset of only six objects. A broader benchmark across diverse categories, complex topologies, and varying mesh resolutions is necessary to demonstrate generalizability.

Crucial implementation details regarding the extraction and spatial alignment of the edited region mesh are missing: it is unclear how the generated 3D component is segmented and aligned/scaled to the source mesh coordinate frame prior to Boolean operations (i.e., whether this step is fully automated or requires manual artist intervention).

Heavy reliance on a proprietary closed-source platform (MeshyAI API) for image-to-3D generation hinders exact reproducibility and raises questions regarding latency and deterministic evaluation; demonstrating the pipeline with open-source models (e.g., Hunyuan3D or CraftsMan3D) is needed.

Evaluation relies solely on 2D rendered image metrics (CLIP similarity and no-reference image quality metrics). The paper lacks 3D geometric fidelity evaluations (e.g., surface smoothness, non-manifold checks) and perceptual user studies assessing geometric plausibility and seam noticeability.

Single-view dependency: starting the edit from a single rendered 2D viewpoint inherently limits modifications that span occluded geometry or require omnidirectional geometric alterations across complex 3D structures.

strengths: Pragmatic decomposition of 3D mesh editing: Leveraging state-of-the-art 2D image editors and image-to-3D generators allows the method to avoid the severe degradation and over-simplification commonly seen in SDS- or early MVD-based mesh optimization.
Qualitative results: As seen in Figures 4 and 5, the edited meshes exhibit sharper geometry and cleaner texture integration compared to older baselines like FocalDreamer and MagicClay.
Versatility in editing modes: The framework naturally accommodates multiple front-ends, including drag-based editing (via LightningDrag) in addition to text-guided editing.
weaknesses: Severely limited evaluation benchmark: The quantitative and qualitative evaluations are conducted on a dataset containing only six objects (Section 4.1). A sample size of six meshes is insufficient to demonstrate statistical significance, robustness across varied topologies, or reliability across diverse mesh categories.

Missing critical technical details regarding alignment and extraction: The pipeline heavily depends on aligning the generated mesh $M_e$ with the target mesh $M_t$, and on extracting the edited sub-mesh $M_r$ (Section 3.1 and 3.2.1). However, because image-to-3D models (such as MeshyAI) output meshes in arbitrary canonical coordinate frames, scales, and poses, the paper fails to explain how 3D registration, scaling, and part extraction are performed (e.g., whether this requires manual user intervention or automated heuristics).

Unfair baseline comparison and attribution of gains: The baselines compared against (FocalDreamer, MagicClay, Instant3dit) rely on older 2D/3D diffusion backends, whereas the proposed method relies on FLUX Kontext and a closed-source commercial platform (MeshyAI). It is unclear how much of the visual quality improvement stems from the proposed Poisson fusion versus the generative capability of MeshyAI. A fair comparison would test existing fusion/stitching baselines (e.g., classical Poisson mesh editing [55], Alpha-blending, or OpenVDB union) on the same generated assets.

Heuristic Poisson normal blending: Applying standard 2D Poisson image editing (PIE) independently to normal maps across arbitrary viewpoints produces multi-view inconsistent target normals $n_p^i$. Relying on an implicit neural SDF to smooth out inconsistencies lacks formal geometric justification.

Lack of 3D-specific metrics and user study: The quantitative evaluation relies exclusively on 2D image-based metrics (CLIP similarity, NIQE, NIMA). There are no geometric preservation metrics (e.g., Chamfer distance or normal consistency on preserved regions to verify non-destructive editing), mesh quality metrics (manifoldness, aspect ratio, self-intersections), or perceptual user studies.

strengths: Decomposing 3D mesh editing into 2D image editing, image-to-3D mesh generation, and seamless local fusion is an intuitive and practical workflow that bypasses common stability issues in direct SDS-based 3D mesh editing.

The qualitative results displayed in Figures 1, 4, and 5 show visually coherent additions (e.g., adding wings, cat head, tails) with noticeably fewer geometric artifacts along boundaries compared to the selected baselines.

Formulating geometric blending via a hybrid SDF/Mesh representation supervised by Poisson-blended normal maps provides an effective way to resolve harsh mesh Boolean seams without excessive vertex smoothing.
The demonstration of extending the framework from text prompts to drag-based manipulation (via LightningDrag) highlights useful interaction flexibility.
weaknesses: The experimental evaluation is severely limited in scale: the quantitative benchmark is evaluated on only six objects (Section 4.1). Reporting quantitative metrics (CLIP, NIQE, NIMA) over six instances lacks statistical significance and makes it difficult to assess generalization across diverse mesh topologies and geometries.

Critical pipeline steps are underspecified and appear to require unstated manual intervention: Section 3.1 states 'we extract the components within the editing region to form the edited region mesh' and Section 3.2.1 states 'We align the edited reference mesh Me with Mt', but the paper never explains how extraction and 3D spatial alignment/scaling are performed. Since image-to-3D models (e.g., MeshyAI) output meshes in arbitrary canonical coordinate frames and scales, achieving accurate alignment without explicit automated registration or human intervention is non-trivial.

Reliance on proprietary, closed-source commercial tools (MeshyAI) significantly hinders reproducibility and obscures attribution: it is difficult to isolate whether the visual fidelity stems from the proprietary generation/texturing backend of MeshyAI or the proposed Poisson fusion pipeline.

Baseline fairness and breadth of comparison are problematic: CraftMesh is compared against older text-driven SDS/MVD baselines (MagicClay, FocalDreamer), whereas CraftMesh leverages state-of-the-art 2D image editing (FLUX) and feed-forward image-to-3D reconstruction. Baselines that operate on image-guided 3D editing or masked 3D reconstruction (e.g., MaskedLRM) are discussed in related work but omitted from the experimental comparison.
Lack of qualitative user studies and geometric fidelity evaluations (e.g., Chamfer distance or normal consistency on preserved regions to verify that non-edited areas are strictly uncorrupted).

strengths: Pragmatic and effective decomposition: By decoupling 3D mesh editing into 2D image manipulation, native single-image 3D mesh generation, and local geometric/textural fusion, the framework bypasses the slow convergence, multi-face artifacts, and quality bottlenecks of direct 3D SDS or MVD optimization.

Clever 2D-to-3D Poisson fusion formulation: Performing Poisson normal blending in multi-view 2D space to guide neural SDF optimization bypasses the high computational complexity of 3D volumetric Poisson solvers ($O(n^3)$ vs. $O(kn^2)$) while naturally regularizing geometric seams and discontinuities across disparate topologies.

Well-designed texture harmonization module: The combination of gradient consistency (Eq. 7), soft boundary distance weighting (Eq. 8), and KDE-based color distribution matching (Eq. 11) effectively resolves the color distribution shift and visible seams typical of independently generated 3D textures.

Strong qualitative results and versatility: Visual comparisons against FocalDreamer, MagicClay, Instant3dit, and VoxHammer show noticeably crisper details and better preserved unedited geometry. Demonstrating text-driven editing alongside drag-based editing (via LightningDrag) highlights broad applicability.

Comprehensive ablations: The ablation study clearly isolates the relative impact of normal blending, texture harmonization loss terms, and verifies framework agnosticism across multiple 3D backbones (Trellis, Hunyuan3D 2.5, MeshyAI).
weaknesses: Under-specified 3D alignment and extraction details: The manuscript states that the edited region mesh is extracted and aligned with the original mesh using prior work [58], but lacks critical details on how canonical scale, translation, and rotation discrepancies inherent to monocular image-to-3D generators are resolved, and whether this step requires manual intervention or is fully automated.

Single-view viewpoint dependency and occlusions: Because the generation relies on a single rendered reference image, it is unclear how the pipeline handles edits that extend across large angles or self-occluded geometries (e.g., wrap-around modifications).

Reliance on commercial closed APIs in default setup: The primary quantitative results and default setup utilize MeshyAI (a commercial API), which poses reproducibility challenges over time, even though open-source backends (Trellis, Hunyuan3D) are ablated.

Evaluation lacks perceptual user studies: Quantitative validation relies exclusively on automated metrics (CLIP similarity, NIQE, NIMA), which often correlate poorly with 3D structural coherence and physical plausibility. A rigorous human preference study would significantly strengthen the empirical claims.

strengths: Practical and effective system design: By decomposing 3D mesh editing into 2D image editing, single-image 3D mesh generation, and local seamless fusion, the framework bypasses the multi-view inconsistency and over-smoothing issues inherent to direct SDS-based or purely MVD-based mesh optimization.

Efficient 2D-guided geometry refinement: Guiding the hybrid SDF/mesh refinement through 2D Poisson-blended surface normal maps provides an elegant way to resolve geometric seams without solving computationally prohibitive 3D volumetric Poisson equations.

Well-designed texture harmonization: The integration of gradient propagation, soft boundary distance attenuation, and kernel density estimation (KDE)-based color distribution matching successfully prevents tone discrepancies and visible texture boundaries.

High visual fidelity and versatility: Qualitative comparisons show noticeably cleaner, sharper, and more semantically aligned modifications than existing baselines (e.g., FocalDreamer, MagicClay, Instant3dit), with successful demonstration across both text-driven edits and drag-based manipulation.
weaknesses: Mathematical typo in Equation (9): The distance-weighting formulation is written as $w_i = (1 - \frac{\delta}{\|p_i^{new} - p_i^{pr}\|_2})^2$. As the distance approaches 0 at the boundary, this term diverges to infinity rather than acting as a standard compact falloff (which is typically $(1 - \frac{\|p_i^{new} - p_i^{pr}\|_2}{\delta})^2$ for distances less than $\delta$).

Missing details on alignment, registration, and region extraction: The paper states that the edited region mesh is extracted and aligned with the original mesh according to [58], but lacks operational clarity. It remains unclear whether user intervention (e.g., manual rigid alignment, scaling, or 3D bounding box selection) is required to position the newly generated part before Boolean operations, especially given that single-image 3D generators typically output shapes in arbitrary canonical frames.

Multi-view consistency of independent 2D Poisson blends: Normal blending via Poisson Image Editing (Eq. 4) is performed independently per viewpoint. While the neural SDF acts as a regularizer, the manuscript does not analyze potential failure modes when 2D boundary edits from disparate views geometrically contradict each other or suffer from occlusions.

Lack of human perceptual evaluation: The quantitative assessment relies entirely on CLIP similarities and no-reference image quality scores (NIQE/NIMA). For localized editing and seamless boundary integration, a rigorous user study evaluating perceptual seam visibility, artifact rate, and overall preference against baselines would offer much stronger empirical support.

strengths: Well-motivated hybrid formulation: Reformulating 3D mesh editing into a 2D image edit, single-view 3D generation, and seamless local fusion effectively avoids the severe over-smoothing, distortion, and multi-view drift common in direct SDS-based or multi-view diffusion optimization pipelines.

Efficient Poisson Normal Blending: Blending rendered 2D surface normals via classical Poisson image editing and transferring the resulting gradients to a hybrid SDF/Mesh representation avoids the high computational overhead of 3D volumetric Poisson solvers while overcoming the topological rigidity and gradient discontinuity issues of classical mesh coordinate blending.

Effective Texture Harmonization: The combination of gradient propagation, soft boundary distance weighting, and distribution-aware color alignment via kernel density estimation (KDE) successfully mitigates color mismatch and visible seams between the synthesized insert and preserved mesh surfaces.

Compelling visual results and versatility: Qualitative comparisons against FocalDreamer, MagicClay, Instant3dit, and VoxHammer demonstrate visibly sharper geometric details, better preservation of unedited regions, and superior visual harmony. Furthermore, the demonstrated extension to drag-based manipulation highlights practical workflow flexibility.

Ablation studies thoroughly validate the individual impact of the geometric blending module, each loss term in the texture harmonization objective, and multiple generative backends (Trellis, Hunyuan3D 2.5, MeshyAI).
weaknesses: Lack of 3D-specific quantitative evaluation: The quantitative assessment relies entirely on 2D rendered image metrics (CLIPsim, CLIPdir, NIQE, NIMA). Standard 3D geometry metrics—such as Chamfer Distance / F-score on the unedited regions to verify faithful structural preservation, or mesh curvature / surface normal continuity across the boundary seam—are missing.

Reliance on commercial/closed-source backends in primary results: The main quantitative and qualitative results heavily utilize MeshyAI, a commercial proprietary tool. While open backends (Hunyuan3D 2.5 and Trellis) are evaluated in the ablation table, the main paper should clarify whether reproducible open-source generation models achieve the same level of boundary alignment and fidelity without commercial API dependencies.

Ambiguity in 3D alignment and component extraction: Section 3.1 and Section 3.2.1 state that the edited region mesh is extracted and aligned with the original mesh according to prior work [58]. The paper lacks technical details on how automatic, robust, or user-dependent this 3D extraction and spatial alignment step is, especially when complex topological changes or severe scale shifts occur.

Viewpoint dependence and occlusion limits: Because the editing workflow originates from a single 2D rendered reference image, edits that wrap around complex 3D objects or require alterations in occluded areas are fundamentally constrained by the single-view 2D editor and single-image-to-3D lifting backend.

Absence of a perceptual user study: Since aesthetic harmony, identity preservation, and boundary naturalness are central claims of the work, a standardized user preference study comparing against baseline methods would have provided stronger empirical backing.
